title: Query-Conditioned Marginals for OT-Based Context Compression: An Empirical Investigation

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to make optimal-transport context compression query-aware, ensuring that capacity is not wasted on task-irrelevant tokens. Paper [9] ("QUITO: Accelerating Long-Context Reasoning through Query-Guided Context Compression") contains a substantively equivalent purpose. QUITO explicitly focuses on query-guided attention compression, leveraging the query to filter out irrelevant information, which aligns with the goal of query-aware context compression.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves QCap-OT, which modifies the OT sender marginals in Sinkhorn-based ComprExIT using query-anchor similarity, without retraining or adding parameters. Paper [20] ("Accelerated Sinkhorn Algorithms for Partial Optimal Transport") discusses partial optimal transport and Sinkhorn-based methods, but it does not address query-anchor similarity or reweighting sender marginals based on query relevance. Paper [9] ("QUITO") uses query-guided attention compression but does not employ optimal transport or Sinkhorn-based methods. No prior paper combines query-aware reweighting with Sinkhorn-based OT in this manner. Thus, the mechanism is uncovered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves statistical indistinguishability from vanilla ComprExIT across all metrics (F1 delta approximately 0, p > 0.05). Paper [9] ("QUITO") uses a similar evaluation design, comparing its query-guided compression method against baseline methods using standard metrics to validate performance. The statistical comparison framework aligns with the evaluation design of the contribution, making this facet covered.

### Domain
The domain is LLM context compression. Papers [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [6], [7], [8], [9], and [24] all address LLM context compression, albeit with different methods or sub-problems. This establishes that the domain is covered.
